clue.text: Absolutely certain to be above zero

definitions.meaning: someone with no doubt at all is sure
a number greater than nought, as opposed to negative

explanation.definitionFit: Being sure of something and a number exceeding nought share one word in English.

clue.text: Dejected when ejected

definitions.meaning: thrown out, as a batter dismissed in baseball or cricket

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both upset and dismissed from play.

clue.text: Marine animal might be a parasite

definitions.meaning: a simple sea creature with a porous body
a scrounger who lives off others

explanation.definitionFit: The porous sea creature and a freeloading scrounger share one word.

clue.text: Sing a round with goblin

definitions.meaning: to sing a part-song in a round, an old sense
an ugly creature of Scandinavian folklore

explanation.definitionFit: An old verb for singing in turn and the folklore monster share one spelling.

clue.text: Five give an allowance for the itinerant

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
taken as written
a grant is an allowance of money

explanation.surface: Five people award a sum of money to a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp moving from place to place with no settled home.

clue.text: At home inside that protective head gear

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece sits within the letters of the other word

parts.note: taken as written
IN is the usual crossword word for being at home

explanation.surface: A helmet worn about the house, described as that bit of protective headwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' looks like part of the scene, but it is the inserted piece, and 'inside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal helmet worn by soldiers or air-raid wardens is protective headwear.

clue.text: Thought is led without being considered perfect

parts.note: an idea is a thought

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside says the following word wraps around the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An idea is followed without being regarded as flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', so the container signal is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: To idealise is to regard as flawless, so this means seen as ideal and without fault.

clue.text: He would almost get the greedy pig, this prickly fellow

parts.note: he would contracts to he'd

indicators.note: almost says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
a hog is a greedy pig

explanation.surface: He would nearly catch the greedy pig, this spiky character.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spiny mammal that rolls into a ball is a prickly creature.

clue.text: All in good order, so pack it up before finding quarters in Norfolk town

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in says the compass points go inside the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk
north and east are quarters of the compass, N and E

explanation.surface: Everything is neat, so pack it in before reaching lodgings in a Norfolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' works as a reversal because this is a down clue; 'in' is the container signal. Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatness is the state of having everything in its proper place.

clue.text: Assiduous in ensuring nothing enters through this way

indicators.note: enters says the zero goes into the middle of the following word

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone careful makes sure no rubbish gets in by this route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts O inside THROUGH, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A diligent, painstaking worker is careful and complete in what they do.

clue.text: Led the way to a goal?

definitions.text: Led the way to a goal?

parts.words: Led the way to a goal?
parts.note: means went in front, but a footballer also scores by nodding the ball into the net

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means led, and in football it means scored with the head.

clue.text: Am getting around to the smallest thing

indicators.note: getting around says the first word goes round the second

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: I'm getting round to the tiniest detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Once thought indivisible, it is the tiniest particle of matter.

clue.text: It's discourteous if gun is fired at everyone by a worker!

indicators.note: a gun that is fired goes off, so its letters are set off into a new order

parts.note: everyone means all
the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: Shooting at people alongside a labourer would be rude indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is fired' is the anagram signal on the gun alone; the rest is a plain charade, with 'It's' just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A man lacking chivalry towards women is impolite and rude.

clue.text: Fail to tell the truth in being unable to get up

parts.note: to fail to tell the truth is to lie
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fibs while too tired to rise from bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A morning spent staying late in bed is time when one does not rise.

clue.text: Part of the hand is restricted by foot

indicators.note: restricted by says the first piece is held inside the second

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bit of one's hand is hemmed in by one's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted by' is the container signal: the foot abbreviation hems in the two-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: The hand clenched tight with the fingers curled in is a punching shape.

clue.text: Very emphatic little sister — about design

indicators.note: about says the word for design goes around the short word for a sister

parts.note: intent is a design or purpose
sis is a shortened form of sister

explanation.surface: A kid sister keeps going on and on about a pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal: the word for design wraps the short sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Insisting firmly means demanding something forcefully and repeatedly.

clue.text: People who know a lot take their beds for luck!

parts.note: MAs are Masters of Arts, graduates presumed learned
cots are small beds

explanation.surface: Learned people carry their beds around as good-luck charms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is only a link joining MAS and COTS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are charms or creatures kept for good fortune, like a team's emblem animal.

clue.text: Brilliant star attacked by angry high class dog

indicators.note: angry says the letters are worked up into a new order

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A bright star is set upon by a furious posh hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angry' rearranges STAR with U and CUR. The definition is 'Brilliant', the clue word 'star' doubling as fodder in a loose semi-&lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth-brightest star in the night sky is the brilliant one in Bootes.

clue.text: Keep notes on someone who is held

parts.note: to detain is to keep someone
E is a musical note, so two of them are EE

explanation.surface: Someone keeps notes on a person in custody.
explanation.definitionFit: A person kept in custody, often without trial, is a prisoner.

clue.text: Film's error showing how fisherman hauls up catch

parts.note: a reel is a spool of film, the 's being 'has' joining the next piece
a sin is a wrong or error

explanation.surface: A movie's blunder shows how an angler lands a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler winds the line onto the spool to bring the fish to the bank.

clue.text: Nominate, being rather mean about it

indicators.note: about here signals the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Picking someone, being somewhat unkind about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to put them forward, to call them by title for a post.

clue.text: Informed that it's not good to point

parts.note: not good means bad
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone was told it is rude to point at people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, not pointing a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: The old past tense of bid means told or ordered someone.

clue.text: Reason to ease cub out

indicators.note: out says the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A reason to coax a young bear out of its den.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction introduces a cause, the reason why something happened.

clue.text: Woodland gods are moving around in isle

indicators.note: moving around says the letters shift into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Forest deities are wandering about an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Silenus and his kind were satyr-like spirits of the woods in Greek myth.

clue.text: Black mood induced when girl returns across the R Atlantic perhaps

parts.note: jet is a deep black

indicators.note: returns says the word is read backwards

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A gloomy mood after a girl flies back over the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns GAL into LAG. The rest of the clue describes the cause: flying across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness after a long flight across time zones is a weary state of mind.

clue.text: Catches a bit of a knock going in the back way

indicators.note: going in says the knock is placed inside the reversed road
back says the word for way is read from right to left

parts.note: ST, street, is a common abbreviation for a way or road
a rap is a knock

explanation.surface: Something gets caught when a bit of a knock comes in by the rear entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal on the way abbreviation, and 'going in' the container signal; 'a bit of' is padding in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices for snaring animals, or the verb for snaring them, mean catches.

clue.text: Nothing nice made into vegetable salad

indicators.note: made into says the letters are reworked into something new

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dull salad is turned into something good.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture of diced vegetables, a dish of chopped veg, is a kind of salad.

clue.text: First basses performed duet for their opening work

indicators.note: performed says the letters are put on in a new arrangement
first says only the opening letter of basses is used

explanation.surface: Bass singers sang a duet for their premiere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' gives B; 'performed' rearranges B with DUET.
explanation.definitionFit: A first public appearance or first piece of work is an opening performance.

clue.text: The older guide has a right to offend

parts.note: to anger someone is to offend them

explanation.surface: A senior guide has the right to upset people.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British Guide movement, a Ranger was the senior section for older girls.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Girl Guides the senior branch for older members bore this title.

clue.text: No sound from this weight lifting equipment

definitions.meaning: a bell that is mute makes no noise
a short bar with weights on each end for exercise

explanation.definitionFit: A silent bell and the gym weight share one name.

clue.text: A set is split up to allow for an afternoon rest

indicators.note: split up says these letters are broken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A matching set is divided to make time for a midday snooze.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a midday nap after lunch.

clue.text: Furious to notice a particular object

parts.note: to notice is to see
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Someone is angry to spot a certain item.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling with rage is how an enraged person is described.
